  • 128 Time Crystals
  • 64 Blackcoin
  • 32 Void
  • 4,096 Temporal Flux

The Core Effect

The upgrade grants you a powerful active ability: the option to force a Blackcoin market crash at the cost of 1 Time Crystal.

Strategic Value: Market Manipulation

Normally, Blackcoin (bcoin) acts as a speculative asset that you buy and sell from the Leviathans (Elders) in exchange for Relics. Its market price naturally fluctuates over time. Additionally, simply holding blackcoins in your inventory provides a +10% bonus to your kittens’ happiness.

However, the Invisible Black Hand lets you actively manipulate the bcoin market to exponentially grow your Relic stockpile:

  1. Force the Crash: Pay a Time Crystal to instantly crash the market, driving the price of Blackcoin down to its absolute floor.
  2. Buy Low: Use your Relics to buy up a massive amount of Blackcoin at this rock-bottom price.
  3. Sell High: Wait as the market “smoothly” recovers and the price rises back up. Once bcoin peaks, trade it all back to the Leviathans for a massive, multiplied return on your original Relic investment.

This “buy-low, sell-high” cycle is one of the fastest ways to generate hundreds of thousands of Relics in the late game.

item.title: Solar Satellites
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Solar Satellites is a highly useful Workshop upgrade that fundamentally changes how your Satellites interact with your power grid.

Here is a breakdown of its prerequisites, costs, and effects:

  • Prerequisites and Cost: To unlock the Solar Satellites upgrade, you must first research the Orbital Engineering technology. Purchasing the upgrade in the Workshop costs 225,000 Science and 750 Alloy.
  • The Effect: By default, every Satellite you deploy in Cath orbit consumes 1 Watt of energy. The Solar Satellites upgrade completely reverses this, transforming your Satellites into dedicated power generators. After purchasing it, each Satellite will instead permanently generate 1 Watt of energy.
  • The Trade-off: The only minor restriction is that once this upgrade is purchased, your Satellites become permanently active and can no longer be toggled off. However, since they are now feeding power into your grid rather than draining it, there is virtually no reason you would ever want to turn them off.

Ultimately, this upgrade provides a massive net positive for your late-game energy grid, effectively resulting in a +2 energy swing for every single Satellite you own!

It represents the instability of time as you attempt to carry resources across different timelines.

How Distortion Works

Distortion is primarily a byproduct of Temporal Paradoxes. When you have Chronospheres, you can carry resources through a reset. However, if you have Void Resonators and certain Paradox upgrades, your game generates “Temporal Paradoxes” (indicated by a purple notification).

  • The Resource Penalty: High levels of Distortion/Paradoxes can cause your resource production to fluctuate or stall.
  • The Paradox Reset: Every time a paradox occurs, you gain a small amount of Void, but you also increase your Distortion level.

Key Upgrades Related to Distortion

As you progress into the “Dark Future” (Year 40,000+), managing Distortion becomes a full-time job for your kittens:

  • [Temporal Accelerators]: These increase the rate at which time passes but also increase the likelihood of paradoxes.
  • [Rectilinear Pitcher]: This upgrade helps mitigate the negative effects of Distortion, allowing your timeline to remain more stable even when carrying massive amounts of resources.
  • [Void]: Paradoxes are the primary way to generate Void in the mid-game. You actually want some level of Distortion/Paradoxes to occur so you can harvest Void for Chronotheology upgrades.

Strategic Impact

  1. Void Farming: Early on, you trigger paradoxes (and thus Distortion) intentionally to get enough Void for your first Obelisks or Nexus.
  2. Stability: In very long runs, Distortion can become a nuisance. You eventually build Mausoleums and other structures to stabilize the timeline.
  3. Flux: Distortion interacts with Temporal Flux. If your Distortion is too high, your ability to “Shatter Crystals” to skip years becomes less efficient.

  • Ratio Reduction: When stacked with earlier upgrades—Ironwood (-50%), Concrete (-30%), and Unobtainium (-25%)—this brings the Hut price ratio down to approximately 1.289.
  • Population Scaling: This reduction allows you to build approximately 23% more Huts than was possible with Unobtainium Huts alone. For instance, a player who previously capped at 50 Huts could reach 61 Huts after this upgrade, adding 22 extra kittens to their village.

Strategic Importance

  • The Eludium Era: Purchasing this upgrade typically occurs as you transition into the mid-to-late game, often coinciding with the beginning of the Unicorn Era and the stabilization of unobtainium production at approximately 1 per second.
  • Paragon Farming: Because reset rewards (Paragon and Karma) are calculated based on population, Eludium Huts are essential for “deep runs” where you aim to maximize your total kitten count.
  • Efficiency Considerations: While valuable for long runs, some optimization guides suggest that Eludium Huts may be ignored during short paragon-grinding runs. This is because the additional kittens only improve paragon-per-hour efficiency by about 1% (for example, increasing efficiency from 86% to 86.6%), which may not justify the 125 eludium cost in a fast-reset scenario.
  • Science Cap Synergy: During this era, your science cap must be sufficiently high (around 275k) to purchase the upgrade, which usually requires a significant network of Observatories, Data Centers, and Bio Labs.

item.title: Electrolytic Smelting
item.description:
Electrolytic Smelting is a powerful mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that significantly boosts the output of your terrestrial Smelters.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Metallurgy science.
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 100,000
    • Titanium: 2,000.

Core Effects

This upgrade makes Smelters “twice as effective” by providing a massive boost to their primary outputs:

  • Iron Production: Increases iron yield from Smelters by +95%.
  • Coal Production: Increases coal yield from Smelters (assuming you have the Coal Furnace upgrade) by +95%.

Strategic Importance

  • Doubling Output: Electrolytic Smelting effectively doubles your Smelter production rate for two critical industrial resources.
  • Resource Bottlenecks: This upgrade is essential for scaling your industrial base. Iron is constantly needed for building components and Observatories, while Coal is the primary ingredient for Steel, which becomes a major bottleneck as you approach the Space era.
  • Synergy: It works alongside other Smelter upgrades like Gold Ore (+0.001 gold/tick) and Nuclear Smelters (+0.0015 titanium/tick), transforming simple early-game buildings into advanced multi-resource refineries.

item.title: Railgun
item.description:
The Railgun is a high-tier Workshop upgrade that provides a permanent boost to your civilization’s catpower generation.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Particle Physics science (which requires 185,000 Science and 135 Blueprints).
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 150,000
    • Titanium: 5,000
    • Blueprints: 25.

Core Effects

The Railgun is categorized as a weapon technology for the Hunter job.

  • Catpower Production: It provides a +25% boost to catpower production.
  • Hunter Efficiency: This bonus specifically increases the rate at which Hunter kittens (or Zebras in Iron Will mode) generate catpower.

Strategic Utility

  • Hunting and Trading: By increasing the rate of catpower accumulation, the Railgun allows you to send out more frequent hunting expeditions (for furs, ivory, and unicorns) and perform more trades with other civilizations.
  • Iron Will Mode: It is considered a vital late-game upgrade for Iron Will runs. Since players in this mode cannot use kittens, they rely entirely on Zebras to generate catpower; the Railgun helps overcome the scarcity of this resource for high-level tasks like launching orbital missions.
  • Late-Game Scaling: It is one of the final upgrades in the weapon chain, which includes the Composite Bow (+50% catpower) and Crossbow (+25% catpower).

Challenge Modifier: Pacifism

In the Pacifism challenge (where hunting is disabled), the effectiveness of weapon technologies like the Railgun is significantly penalized. For each completion of the challenge, the effectiveness of the Railgun is reduced by -10% (additive), up to a maximum penalty of -100%.

item.title: Offset_Press
item.description:

  • Unlocked By: You must first research the Combustion technology.
  • Resource Requirements:
    • Science: 100,000

The Offset Press serves as a direct multiplier to the Printing Press upgrade:

  • Production Boost: It makes the Printing Press four times as effective.
  • Manuscript Rate: It increases the passive manuscript generation of active Steamworks from 0.0025 per second to 0.01 manuscripts/sec.
  • Prerequisite: Purchasing this upgrade is required to eventually unlock Photolithography, which further quadruples production to 0.04 manuscripts/sec.

  • Effect: Increases the production bonus derived from kitten skills by 15%.

2. The “Factory Logistics” Workshop Upgrade

This is a high-tier industrial upgrade that is critical for transitioning into the endgame “Shatter Engine.”

    • Concrete: 125.

  • Scaling Bonus: Each Factory built provides a +5% bonus to oil refinement effectiveness (the amount of Kerosene produced from Oil).
  • Multiplicative Stacking: This effectiveness bonus stacks multiplicatively with your global crafting ratio bonuses, allowing for massive Kerosene yields as your industrial base grows.
  • Workshop Interaction: While primarily categorized as a Factory upgrade, it is purchased in the Workshop and listed as improving “Kerosene Crafting”.

  • Fuel for Space Exploration: Kerosene is a critical resource for late-game progression, used as fuel for Spaceports and for sending high-tier space missions like Piscine, Helios, and T-Minus.

  • Infrastructure Synergy: This upgrade transforms Factories from simple crafting boosters into vital components of your energy and fuel supply chain, making large factory networks essential for sustained space operations.

The Flux Condensator is a high-tier Workshop upgrade for the Chronosphere mega-structure that enables the preservation of crafted resources during a game reset.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Prerequisite Technology: It is unlocked by researching Chronophysics, which requires 250,000 Science and 5 Time Crystals.
  • Upgrade Cost: Purchasing the upgrade costs 250 Alloy, 5,000 Unobtainium, and 5 Time Crystals.
  • Persistence: The Flux Condensator upgrade does not carry over across resets; it must be repurchased in every run where you intend to use its effects.

Core Effects and Mechanics

While the Chronosphere normally only preserves a percentage of non-crafted resources, the Flux Condensator extends this ability to include complex materials.

  • Preservation Formula: The amount of each crafted resource preserved is determined by the number of Chronospheres built and the amount held at reset: $1.5 {number of Chronospheres} \sqrt{{resource amount}}$**.
  • Resources Affected: This includes critical materials such as Steel, Alloy, Concrete, Eludium, Gear, Scaffold, Ship, Tanker, Kerosene, Parchment, Manuscript, Compendium, Blueprint, Thorium, and Megalith.
  • Diminishing Returns: Because the formula uses a square root function, the efficiency of resource carryover decreases the more of a resource you have.

Strategic Importance

The Flux Condensator is considered a game-changing upgrade for mid-to-late-game progression loops:

  • Science Storage Carryover: Its most significant benefit is the preservation of Compendiums. Since Compendiums increase maximum science storage, bringing thousands into a new run allows players to hit late-game science caps and unlock advanced technologies in the very first years of a new run.
  • Early Industrial Stability: Bringing over Ships and Scaffolds significantly speeds up early titanium collection and harbour construction, eliminating the early-game trading bottlenecks.
  • Endgame “Positive Resets”: In the deep endgame, the Flux Condensator is mandatory for “positive resets,” where the goal is to start each run with a net profit of materials compared to the previous one.
  • Resource Management: Players are advised to stockpile crafted resources before resetting with this upgrade to maximize the square-root-based yield. For example, having a high crafting ratio before reset is more efficient than waiting to craft resources in the next run.

item.description:

The upgrade provides a multiplicative storage bonus to several buildings:

  • Storage Increase: It increases the maximum amount of wood, minerals, coal, iron, gold, and titanium stored in Warehouses, Barns, Harbours, and Mints by 45%.

  • The “Alloy Era”: Acquiring Alloy Warehouses and Alloy Barns is a major milestone often reached when a player has between 90 and 100 kittens.

By expanding resource caps, Alloy Warehouses allow you to accumulate the massive quantities of materials needed for advanced industrial structures like Factories, Reactors, and early space missions.

Strategic Importance: The First Reset

Concrete Huts is the single most important milestone for determining when to perform your first reset.

  • The 130 Kitten Goal: Without this upgrade, most players cap out around 70–80 kittens. Concrete Huts allows you to push your population to 130–140 kittens.
  • Paragon Farming: Since you earn 1 Paragon for every kitten over 70, reaching 130 kittens guarantees you 60 Paragon upon resetting. This is the recommended amount needed to buy essential Metaphysics upgrades (like Diplomacy and Golden Ratio) for your second run.

Requirements and The “Concrete Era”

Reaching Concrete Huts requires overcoming two main bottlenecks:

  1. Science Cap: The 125,000 Science cost is often higher than your caps allow. You will likely need to build Bio Labs (unlocked by Biology) or craft extensive Compendiums to raise your maximum science limit enough to afford it.
  2. Titanium: The 3,000 Titanium cost requires a robust trade network with the Zebras. You should rely on Trade Ships and Geodesy (if unlocked) to stockpile this Titanium.

Once you purchase Concrete Huts, the strategy is simple: build as many Huts as your storage allows, maximize your population, and then execute the BMF (Backup, Metas, Faith) checklist before resetting.

  • Resource Cost: 50 Concrete.

Core Effects

Unlike the massive +75% boost from Concrete Barns, this upgrade provides a smaller, universal reinforcement to your storage infrastructure:

  • Workshop Upgrade Cost: 500,000 Science, 5 Relics, and 10 Time Crystals.

  • Important Note: Unlike Cryptotheology buildings, Chronoforge upgrades do not carry over through resets. You must rebuild your infrastructure in the Time tab every run.

Core Mechanic: Combusting Time Crystals

The primary function of the Chronoforge is the ability to “Combust Time Crystal” (often called “shattering”).

  • Effect: Instantly skips the game calendar to the beginning of the next Spring.
  • Cost: 1 Time Crystal (Base).
  • Heat Mechanic: Each shatter generates 10 units of Chronoheat. If your current heat exceeds your maximum heat limit, the Time Crystal cost to shatter increases by +1% for every unit of excess heat.

Key Chronoforge Structures

Once the Chronoforge is unlocked, you can purchase several sub-structures in the Time tab to manage heat and improve efficiency:

Structure Cost Function
Chrono Furnace 25 TCs, 5 Relics Increases max heat capacity by 100. It also automatically converts accumulated heat into “fuel” to trigger free time skips.
Time Boiler 25k TCs Expands the heat capacity of Chrono Furnaces by 10 per boiler.
Temporal Accelerator 10 TCs, 1k Relics Improves time-related effects (like Time Impedance and Unicornmancy) by 5%. It also reduces the “lag” associated with mass-shattering.
Resource Retrieval 1k TCs Crucial for the Endgame. Requires Paradox Theory. It allows you to gain 1% of your yearly resource production per level every time you shatter a Time Crystal.

Strategic Utility: The Shatter Engine

The Chronoforge is the engine of the late-game economy (Phase 3/4).

  1. Antimatter Generation: By building Sunlifters and shattering Time Crystals, you can cycle through years rapidly, generating massive amounts of Antimatter (which is produced annually) without waiting for real-time days to pass.
  2. Void Generation: If you have Chronospheres, skipping years forces “Temporal Paradoxes” (Void spawns) to occur more frequently in real-time.
  3. Redmoon Cycling: Players use the Chronoforge to skip “weak” planetary cycles (like Charon) and land specifically on Redmoon or Dune cycles to maximize Unobtainium production for trading.
  4. Infinite Loop: With enough Resource Retrieval levels, a single shatter yields enough Unobtainium/Alicorns to trade or sacrifice for more than 1 Time Crystal. This creates a self-sustaining loop where you can skip time indefinitely.

Standard travel time to the Furthest Ring is approximately 725,200,000 game-days, which is over 16,000 real-world days, though this can be drastically reduced by researching advanced propulsion systems. The Thorium Drive divides travel time by 50, while the Antimatter Drive divides it by 25; researching both reduces travel times by a factor of 75.

Managing fuel for these long-range operations is a critical bottleneck, as missions to the outer reaches of the solar system and beyond require high quantities of Kerosene and Thorium. To sustain these operations, the sources recommend focusing on maximising unobtainium production via Lunar Outposts to craft the Eludium needed for high-tier space structures. Additionally, the USS Mining Vessel Hissmeowra, known as the Planet Cracker, acts as a heavy industrial vessel used to produce Uranium from Dune. Successful long-range progression relies on balancing these mobile assets with terrestrial storage and science capacity.

item.title: Starlink
item.description:
Starlink is a late-game workshop upgrade that enhances the scientific synergy between Bio Labs and Data Centres. It is unlocked after researching the Orbital Engineering technology and requires 175,000 Science, 5,000 Alloy, and 25,000 Oil to purchase.

Mechanical Effects and Synergy

The primary function of Starlink is to increase the maximum science capacity of your colony by linking building counts:

  • Capacity Bonus: Every active Data Centre provides an additional 1% bonus to the maximum science capacity provided by each Bio Lab.
  • Stacking with Uplink: Starlink acts as a follow-up to the Uplink upgrade. While Uplink provides an initial 1% bonus to Bio Lab science per Data Centre (and improves Data Centre caps per Bio Lab), Starlink adds a second 1% modifier, effectively doubling the contribution Bio Labs receive from your Data Centre infrastructure.

Strategic Utility

Scaling the maximum science cap is a critical requirement for late-game progression, as advanced technologies and space missions have resource requirements that eventually exceed base storage limits. Because this bonus is percentage-based and scales with the number of buildings, it allows players to reach the high science thresholds necessary for Exometallurgy (325,000 Science), Tachyon Theory (750,000 Science), and even higher-tier endgame goals.

The Oil Refinery is a critical component for overcoming the oil bottleneck that often occurs before the establishment of high-output space structures.

Strategic Utility

While early-game survival depends on managing production through Farmers and Aqueducts to survive “Cold” winters, Refrigeration becomes available during the Industrial and Space eras. At this stage of development, increasing the catnip “cap” is less about immediate survival and more about resource efficiency.

  • Preventing Waste: Initially, any catnip produced beyond the 5,000-unit starting limit is lost. Expanding this cap allows for a larger buffer during long idle periods or when shifting the workforce entirely into non-food roles like Scholars or Geologists.
  • Refinement Efficiency: Increasing the cap allows players to hold more catnip for mass-conversion into Wood via the “Refine catnip” button, which becomes more efficient after the Catnip Enrichment upgrade.

Think of Refrigeration like upgrading your colony from a standard esky to a professional walk-in freezer; it doesn’t make the catnip grow faster, but it ensures that when your fields are overflowing, you have the room to keep every last leaf fresh for when the winter nosedive hits.

item.title: Register
item.description:

Mechanical Effects

The upgrade automates the optimisation of kitten skills during the assignment process:

  • Skill Prioritisation: When adding kittens to a job, the system automatically selects kittens with the highest relevant experience levels first.

Kittens gain experience over time as they perform specific tasks, progressing through seven skill tiers from Dabbling (0% bonus) to Master (18.75% bonus). Because these bonuses stack multiplicatively with other productivity modifiers, ensuring the right kittens are in the right jobs is vital for maximising resource output.

This is particularly useful for reaching the high Titanium and Science caps required for the Eludium and Relic eras, as terrestrial buildings eventually become prohibitively expensive due to steep price ratios. Proper investment in these upgrades allows Accelerators to provide a substantial percentage of a colony’s total storage, often surpassing the utility of Harbours in the very late game.

Strategic Importance

The Printing Press is a crucial step in resolving the mid-game Manuscript bottleneck, which gates progression to advanced technologies like Theology and Astronomy.

  • Manuscript Generation: Prior to automation, Manuscripts must be manually crafted using scarce resources (Parchment from Furs, acquired through Hunting, and Culture from Amphitheatres/Temples). The Printing Press provides an automated source of Manuscripts, converting the high-cost materials (Coal, Iron, Blueprints) required for Steamworks into sustained cultural output.
  • Technological Progression: While acquiring the necessary materials—including Blueprints and Gears (which require Steel)—to build Steamworks can present its own hurdle, establishing automated Manuscript production allows the player to bypass the tedious and slow process of manual crafting.
  • Challenge Mode: The Printing Press is particularly critical in the Pacifism Challenge, where Hunting is unavailable. Since Hunting is the primary source of Furs (needed to craft Parchment), and therefore Manuscripts, the Pacifism Challenge dictates that the player must rely on Mints (to generate Furs/Ivory) and the Printing Press to get the required Manuscripts for progression.

Further Upgrades

The effectiveness of the Printing Press can be significantly improved by later technologies:

  • Offset Press: This upgrade (unlocked by Combustion) is four times as effective, raising Steamworks output to 0.01 manuscripts/sec.
  • Photolithography: This further upgrade (unlocked by Satellites) increases the printing effectiveness again, raising the rate to 0.04 manuscripts/sec.

  • Prerequisite Technology: Silos is unlocked after researching Ironwood Huts.
  • Cost: Researching the Silos upgrade requires 50,000 Science, 125 Steel, and 5 Blueprints.

2. Key Effects and Functionality

Silos fundamentally changes how resource storage buildings (Barns, Warehouses, and Harbours) function by enabling the storage of Catnip in structures beyond just Barns, and by enhancing the effectiveness of all general storage upgrades.

  • Warehouse Catnip Storage: After Silos is researched, each Warehouse begins to increase maximum Catnip capacity by +750. Warehouses are initially unlocked by researching Construction.
  • Barn Upgrade Bonus Application: Silos causes all storage upgrades that contain the word “barns” in their name (e.g., Expanded Barns, Reinforced Barns, Titanium Barns, Alloy Barns, Concrete Barns, and Concrete Pillars) to apply 25% of their effect to the maximum Catnip capacity as well. This dramatically boosts Catnip storage capacity. For example, the maximum total bonus applied to Catnip storage via this mechanic from all relevant upgrades is $+108.75%$.
  • Warehouse and Harbour Storage Bonus: This same bonus calculation also applies to the Catnip capacity provided by Warehouses and Harbours.

3. Strategic Importance

This upgrade is vital in the mid-game, as managing the Catnip surplus and deficit is a core mechanic of the game.

  • Catnip Stability: While the base Catnip storage capacity starts at 5,000, each Kitten consumes 4.25 Catnip per second. Expanding storage capacity is crucial for surviving harsh Winters, where Catnip production from Catnip Fields can drop by 75% or more. Silos allows the player to overcome storage limits and build up massive stockpiles needed for long-term food security and efficient wood refinement.
  • Technological Progression: The ability to craft this upgrade requires a decent industrial base to produce Steel and acquire Blueprints.

Think of Silos as converting your general storage buildings into food warehouses. Before Silos, only specialised agricultural structures (Barns) could hold your food supply, limiting your stockpile size. With Silos, every Warehouse and Harbour you build can now help keep your community fed, turning industrial storage into emergency reserves.

item.title: Workshop_Automation
item.description:
The term “Workshop Automation” refers to a specific Workshop upgrade associated with the Steamworks building in Kittens Game.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Workshop Automation upgrade:

  • Prerequisite Technology: This upgrade is unlocked by researching the Machinery technology.
  • Cost: To acquire Workshop Automation, you must spend 10,000 Science and 25 Gears.
  • Effect/Function: Once purchased, the upgrade converts small quantities of craftable resources into materials when they are near their storage limit.
    • Specifically, Workshop Automation converts 2% plus 2% times the number of Steamworks of wood into beams and minerals into slabs when that resource is at 98% of its storage cap.
    • This conversion occurs once per year (i.e., in the Spring season).
    • The goal of this automation is to help players manage their storage capacity by automatically converting common, capped resources (Wood and Minerals) into more advanced materials (Beams and Slabs).
  • Advanced Form: There is a subsequent upgrade, Advanced Automation, which causes Workshop Automation to be triggered twice per year.
  • Related Upgrade: The Pneumatic Press upgrade further enhances this function by enabling Workshop Automation to also convert Iron into Plates.

In essence, Workshop Automation allows your Steamworks to passively manage resource bottlenecks, ensuring that your basic resources (Wood and Minerals) continue to generate useful craftable materials even when they are approaching their storage limits. This is particularly handy for generating Beams and Slabs without requiring constant manual crafting.

The primary function of AI Bases is to create a multiplicative storage bonus based on your mega-structure population:

  • Effect: Every AI Core you have built increases the effectiveness of your Moon Bases by +10%.
  • Independence from AI Level: Crucially, this bonus is derived strictly from the number of AI Cores owned. It is not affected by your current AI Level, Gigaflops count, or the threat of an AI Apocalypse.

Strategic Synergies

  • Transkittenism Policy: If the Transkittenism policy is active (requiring a Leviathan trade), the bonus provided by AI Bases is further enhanced. Advanced guides indicate that under this policy, the bonus effectively increases to 11% per AI Core.
  • Unobtainium Capacity: AI Bases are a critical component of the deep late-game “Chrono-Engine.” Because Moon Bases are one of only two structures that provide Unobtainium storage (the other being Cryostations), scaling them with AI Cores is essential for reaching the 8.14 billion Unobtainium cap required to build 100 Chronospheres for “positive resets”.
  • Antimatter Management: Since the upgrade itself costs 7,500 Antimatter and requires AI Cores (which consume significant energy), players typically prioritize this after they have stabilized their Sunlifter production and Containment Chamber storage.

By combining a large number of AI Cores with the AI Bases upgrade, your Moon Bases—which initially provide only 150 Unobtainium storage each—can scale to support the massive resource requirements of the endgame.

  • Enhanced UI and Management: The upgrade provides more detailed information via the pollution indicator in the Science tab and adds +/- buttons to all polluting buildings. Strategic Utility

Managing pollution is critical because high levels of atmospheric CO2 negatively impact several areas of your village:

  • Production Penalties: High pollution reduces catnip production, which can lead to kitten starvation.
  • Civilian Penalties: It decreases kitten happiness and slows down the arrival speed of new kittens.
  • Religious Penalties: Eventually, extreme pollution can reduce the Solar Revolution bonus for certain resources.

While some pollution is considered inevitable, Carbon Sequestration is one of the few active methods to keep levels below the ~1,000 ppm threshold, where negative effects are generally negligible.

  • Time Crystals: 5

Core Effects and Functionality

The upgrade provides two primary benefits to your automated workforce:

  1. Improved Engineer Know-how: It provides a flat +2 know-how bonus to all five classes of Engineers. While other upgrades like AI Engineers or Space Engineers provide higher specific class bonuses, Chronoengineers ensure a baseline efficiency boost across the entire job spectrum.
  2. Work During Time Skips: This is the upgrade’s most unique feature. It enables Engineers to continue their automated crafting tasks even when you are combusting Time Crystals to skip years.

Synergy with Resource Retrieval

When a time skip occurs, the amount of crafting performed by Chronoengineers is dictated by your Resource Retrieval level.

  • Automated Conversion: Just as Resource Retrieval allows you to collect a percentage of your annual production during a skip, Chronoengineers allow your Engineers to “catch up” on their work for that skipped period.
  • Material Consumption: It is important to note that this automated crafting consumes the required materials just like standard crafting; it does not produce resources “for free” during the skip.

This upgrade is essential for maintaining a stable industrial output during the late-game “shatter engine” phase, ensuring that your refined resource stocks (like Steel, Plate, or Alloy) continue to grow alongside your raw materials as you skip through the centuries.

  • Resources Affects: This multiplier applies to your maximum Wood, Minerals, Coal, Iron, Gold, and Titanium.

  • Resource Cost: 35 Concrete and 1,250 Titanium.
  • Prerequisite: You must have researched Mechanization and purchased the Concrete Pillars upgrade first.

Strategic Utility

  • The Concrete Suite: This upgrade is part of the critical trio of concrete upgrades (Pillars, Barns, Warehouses). While Concrete Barns offers a higher percentage boost (+75%), Concrete Warehouses is essential because it scales your Harbors, which become your primary source of storage in the mid-to-late game.
  • Pre-Reset Push: Players often purchase this alongside Concrete Huts to maximize their storage limits, allowing them to build a few extra Log Houses or Mansions to squeeze out more kittens (and thus more Paragon) before resetting.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 10,000.
  • Resource Cost: 50 Steel.
  • Prerequisite: Researching the Steel technology is mandatory before this upgrade appears.

Effects on Hunting

The primary function of Steel Armour is to increase the hunting bonus for your kittens (or Zebras in Iron Will mode).

  • Hunting Bonus: It provides a flat +0.5 bonus to hunting effectiveness.
  • Additive Stacking: This bonus is additive with other hunting upgrades. For example, if you have already researched Bolas (+1.0) and Hunting Armour (+2.0), adding Steel Armour brings your total hunting bonus to 3.5.
  • Yield Increase: This upgrade increases the basic fur and ivory hunting amounts by approximately 40–50%.
  • Expected Results: With Bolas, Hunting Armour, and Steel Armour active, the expected yield per hunt is approximately 153.25 fur and 47.94 ivory.

Technical Mechanics

Because Steel Armour provides a non-integral bonus (+0.5), it causes the probability distribution for hunting resources to become non-uniform. When calculating the amount of furs or gold acquired, the game generates a random integer range; a non-integral hunting bonus allows for the possibility of generating the next highest integer in the range, though with half the probability of the other integers.

Strategic Utility

Steel Armour is essential for scaling your cultural engine in the mid-game. Higher fur yields allow for more rapid crafting of Parchment, which is the foundational material for Manuscripts and Compendiums. Additionally, increased ivory yields are critical for trading with the Nagas to resolve mineral bottlenecks.

Thorium Reactors is a high-tier late-game Workshop upgrade that enhances the power output of your standard Reactor buildings. It represents a shift towards more advanced nuclear fuels to meet the escalating energy demands of space exploration and artificial intelligence.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 400,000.
  • Resource Cost: 10,000 Thorium.
  • Prerequisite Technology: You must first research the Thorium science technology, which is unlocked after Orbital Engineering.

Core Effects and Mechanics

The upgrade allows your existing Reactors to utilise Thorium as a secondary, more potent fuel source:

  • Energy Boost: It provides a +25% increase to the energy production of every Reactor. Given that a base Reactor produces 10 Watts, this upgrade typically adds +2.5 Watts per building.
  • Fuel Consumption: This boost comes at the cost of Thorium consumption, which is depleted at a rate of 0.05 to 0.25 units per tick depending on your current level of automation and research.
  • Toggleable Functionality: Like many advanced industrial buildings, the Thorium consumption (and its associated energy bonus) can be toggled on or off to manage resource levels.

Strategic Importance

  • Supporting the Endgame Grid: Thorium Reactors are essential for powering energy-heavy structures such as AI Cores, Entanglement Stations, and Terraforming Stations.
  • Antimatter Generation: A common strategy is to only activate Thorium Reactors during time skips to ensure a positive energy state. This is vital because Sunlifters only produce antimatter if your energy production is positive when the year changes.
  • Efficiency Upgrades: Once Thorium Reactors are active, you should prioritise the Enriched Thorium upgrade. This reduces the fuel consumption of your reactors by 25%, allowing your Thorium stockpiles to last significantly longer.

In specialised challenge runs like Iron Will, where kittens are unavailable, the energy boost from Thorium Reactors is often a mandatory requirement for reaching the high power thresholds needed for deep-space missions.

item.title: Titanium Axe
item.description:
The Titanium Axe is a mid-to-late-game Workshop upgrade that provides a significant boost to your wood production infrastructure.

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 38,000.
  • Resource Cost: 10 Titanium.
  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Navigation science technology.

Core Effects

The Titanium Axe is described as being “indestructible” and provides a flat +50% bonus to Woodcutter output (woodRatio). It is part of a linear progression of woodcutting tools, following the Steel Axe and preceding the Alloy Axe.

The Titanium Axe is described as being “indestructible” and provides a flat +50% bonus to Woodcutter output (woodRatio). It is part of a linear progression of woodcutting tools, following the Steel Axe and preceding the Alloy Axe.

Strategic Utility

  • Multiplicative Scaling: A critical strategic detail of the axe upgrade chain is that its bonuses are multiplicative with the production boost provided by Lumber Mills. This makes the upgrade far more impactful than simple additive bonuses, allowing wood production to scale effectively as construction costs for advanced buildings like Harbours and Observatories rise.
  • Transition into the Titanium Era: Because this upgrade requires Titanium, it serves as one of the first practical uses for the resource after you begin trading with the Zebras.
  • Resolving Wood Bottlenecks: Wood is often a major bottleneck in the mid-game for building Ships and Scaffolds; acquiring the Titanium Axe is essential for maintaining the velocity of your expansion during the “Titanium buildup” phase.

    • 200k Science
    • 350 Unobtainium
    • 15k Titanium

3. Infrastructure Requirements to Reach It

Reaching Unobtainium Huts requires establishing a foothold in Space and expanding your resource caps:

  • Unobtainium Storage Cap: Base Unobtainium storage is only 150. You must build at least 1 Moon Base (which requires 50 Unobtainium, 70k Oil capacity, 9,500 Titanium, and 250 Concrete) to raise your storage capacity past the 350 Unobtainium threshold needed for the upgrade.
  • Unobtainium Generation: Requires Lunar Outposts to convert Uranium into Unobtainium.
  • Uranium Supply: Because Lunar Outposts consume Uranium rapidly, relying on Orbital Geodesy (Quarries produce Uranium) or trading Titanium with Dragons is strongly recommended to keep Outposts running.
  • Starcharts & Oil: You will need roughly 2,100 Starcharts to fund the prerequisite space missions (Orbital Launch and Moon Mission) and an Oil capacity of at least 70k.

4. Strategic Role and Reset Checkpoint

  • Progression Milestone: Early game resets typically peak at Concrete Huts (around 130–150 kittens). Unobtainium Huts serves as the next primary milestone once your Paragon pool and storage multipliers are high enough to comfortably reach Space.
  • Farming Renaissance: A common strategy is to repeat runs pushing to Unobtainium Huts to max out kitten housing, stockpiling Paragon until you can purchase all the core price reduction Metaphysics upgrades through to Renaissance (750 Paragon) before committing to the heavier Eludium and Time Crystal eras.

Upgrade Progression

The Steel Saw is the second tier in the specialized saw lineage:

  1. Reinforced Saw: +2% bonus (Requires Construction).
  2. Steel Saw: +2% bonus (Requires Physics).
  3. Titanium Saw: +1.5% bonus (Requires Steel Saw).
  4. Alloy Saw: +1.5% bonus (Requires Titanium Saw).

Strategic Utility

At this stage of the game, wood production is often a major bottleneck for constructing Observatories, Harbours, and Trade Ships. While individual global multipliers (like Kittens or Magnetos) are generally preferred, the Saw upgrades are highly valued because they are multiplicative with the Axe chain of upgrades (Iron, Steel, Alloy, etc.), providing a necessary foundation for your industrial economy.
